key_insight: Spatial-TTT applies test-time training to streaming video so a model can continuously adapt, selectively store, and organize spatial evidence—enabling persistent spatial intelligence from unbounded visual streams.
problem_solved: How to maintain, update, and compress spatial information from potentially unbounded video streams—selecting, organizing, and retaining relevant spatial cues over time rather than merely increasing context window length.
method: Streaming spatial memory that incrementally accumulates and prunes visual evidence to form a persistent spatial representation.
Online test-time training (self-supervised) that adapts model parameters on incoming frames to align perception with the current environment.
Lightweight selection and update rules that preserve key geometry/semantics while enabling continuous operation without full offline retraining.
impact: Enables systems (robots, AR/VR, mapping) to maintain robust, long-term spatial understanding by adapting on-the-fly to new environments; reduces reliance on large offline datasets and periodic retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: live video stream → TTT adaptation block → streaming spatial memory → downstream task (e.g., mapping/localization)
Timeline/stream graphic showing evidence accumulation, pruning, and model updates over time compared to naive buffering
Before/after qualitative map or scene understanding examples: baseline vs Spatial-TTT
Performance-over-time chart: sustained accuracy or task metric vs baselines that degrade without streaming adaptation
paper_title: Spatial-TTT: Streaming Visual-based Spatial Intelligence with Test-Time Training
paper_authors: Fangfu Liu, Diankun Wu, Jiawei Chi, Yimo Cai, Yi-Hsin Hung
